Subject: Amendment request — additional capacity and usage-credit rollback carve-out

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last month. We're moving ahead with the internal procurement approvals and have two items we need to address via an amendment to the existing MSA + order form (ELR-2025-11):

1) Add 60 reserved GPU nodes (pilot -> production) starting 2026-05-01; term aligned to existing order form.
2) Provider-side request: we need the pricing ladder for the added nodes to be fixed for 12 months.
3) Critical ask: Elara requests a one-time carve-out that prevents Redwood from clawing back previously issued usage credits tied to the pilot if there is a scope/price amendment within 90 days of signature (we want credit stability while we transition).

Can your team draft an amendment and redline the MSA/order form accordingly? We've attached a high-level schedule and forecast (attachment: elara_capacity_schedule.xlsx).

Our procurement window is tight — approval path closes 2026-03-31. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,

Team —

Looping you in on Elara's request (see thread below). They've asked for: 60 reserved nodes (start 5/1), fixed pricing for 12mo, and a 90-day non-clawback carve-out for pilot credits.

Please review Elara_AMEND_v1.docx (attached in the client thread) with focus on:

Karthik — if you can confirm internal ops ETA for provisioning and any surge/burst constraints that should be reflected in acceptance criteria, that would help.

I want legal comments back by end-of-day 3/17 so we can send a revised redline to Elara on 3/18.

Subject: RE: INTERNAL: Elara amendment — please review redline and prioritize carve-out language

Vivek/Team —

Quick read & summary of legal redlines against Elara_AMEND_v1.docx (high level):

1) Capacity + Acceptance (Section 2):
- Proposed addition is straightforward. Recommend adding an "Implementation SLA" subsection: target provisioning date (5/1) with an operations-level acceptance test (sample traffic + 72-hour stability window).

2) Pricing Guarantee (Section 6):
- We can accept a 12-month price guarantee for the new nodes but must preserve a narrow exception for force majeure and regulatory changes. Suggest language that prices "shall not increase except as required by changes in applicable law or with mutual written agreement."

3) Credit carve-out (Section 9):
- We cannot agree to a blanket prohibition on clawbacks for all credit types. Proposed compromise: a 90-day stability window limited to "onboarding and pilot credits explicitly listed in Exhibit A" and excluding credits that were issued in error, for fraud, or where material misrepresentation is later discovered.
- Add a short audit right to allow us to validate whether credits were properly earned (driven by a simple evidence request; Redwood to provide audit findings within 10 business days).

4) Ops / Escrow language:
- If Elara wants explicit guarantees on provisioning timing, include a mutual SLA with limited remedy (service credits) rather than financial penalties. Ops to confirm acceptable credit caps.

I've attached a redlined legal version (redlines_legal_v2.docx) showing the exact suggested language for Section 6 and Section 9. Key suggested fallback phrasing for the credit carve-out: "Credits listed in Exhibit A shall not be reversed by Redwood within ninety (90) days following execution of this Amendment, except where Redwood reasonably determines, following audit, that such credits were issued in error or as a result of fraud or material misrepresentation."

If we can get ops ETA and confirm credit types by EOD 3/17, I'll incorporate final language and we can send to Elara 3/18.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
